method: WebSearch '<process> machine learning / computer vision / robotics' per process; count DISTINCT on-target AI applications (AI applied to THIS process step) vs adjacent (AI on a different step/related domain -- which proves the technique is feasible). R10: report counts. <5 on-target = genuine application white space.
KEY_FINDING_R10: AI penetration VARIES sharply and discriminates. Two 'obvious' labor-intensive targets are ALREADY heavily AI'd (saffron: robots+NeRF+ANN+startups; sericulture: CNN disease detection + ML cocoon-sorting prototype) -> NOT white space. Three are genuinely under-served ON-TARGET (retting endpoint, cork stripping, traditional charcoal-kiln smoke monitoring) while the underlying TECHNIQUE is proven on adjacent tasks -> feasible application gaps. nixtamalization has 1 direct paper (started).

processes.evidence: Engine: 'didn't return papers specifically focused on flax retting endpoint detection.' Adjacent (PROVEN technique, feasible): hyperspectral+ML for flaxseed mechanical-damage (PMC10778999), cannabis drying-quality (PMC11082398), crop disease (MDPI 16/14/6064). The technique (hyperspectral/CV + ML for material-state quality) is mature; applying it to retting-degree endpoint is unexploited.
processes.feasibility_note: HIGH -- hyperspectral+ML material-quality assessment is established; retting endpoint = pectin-degradation state is a natural target

processes.evidence: Engine: cork stripping 'RESISTS automation... no mechanized process; despite periodic attempts.' Existing AI is DOWNSTREAM only: cork-driller feeding (277927174), cork-surface SVM classification. The harvest/stripping step itself is AI-unpenetrated.
processes.feasibility_note: MIXED -- FULL robotic stripping has failed repeatedly (likely infeasible); but a NARROW improvement (CV cork-cambium-boundary / cut-depth guidance ASSISTING the human, or bark-readiness assessment) is plausible. R13: the proposal must be the narrow feasible version, not 'automate stripping'.

processes.evidence: On-target (traditional earth-kiln smoke-stage monitoring): engine notes 'smoke color analysis for direct process control appears limited.' Adjacent (PROVEN/feasible): rotary-kiln burning-state recognition from flame images (S0925231212004201), satellite kiln DETECTION (different task), pyrolysis-yield ML modeling.
processes.feasibility_note: HIGH -- image-based kiln burning-state recognition is proven on rotary kilns; transferring CV smoke-stage classification to traditional earth kilns is feasible

processes.evidence: DIRECT prior art exists: 'Predicting Moisture Content During Maize Nixtamalization Using ML with NIR Spectroscopy' (bioRxiv 2021, SVM, rho 0.852) + RSM optimization of alkaline processing. The exact 'ML + spectroscopy for nixtamalization endpoint' application is already begun.
processes.feasibility_note: feasible BUT application gap is largely CLOSED (direct paper) -> likely Gate-3 fail

processes.evidence: Already AI'd: CNN silkworm disease detection (IEEE 10441723; researchgate 384221299), ML cocoon-sorting prototype with 3 cameras + AI model to discard dead cocoons (PMC9862640). The deliberate already-AI'd contrast.

Already a hot robotics/CV area despite Wikipedia's 'mechanical harvesting is not an option': Dyno Robotics saffron robot (cameras+NeRF), Robotic Saffron startup, ANN flower detection 96-100% (S0168169919302686), multiple harvesting-device papers.
